title: Ex-Assassin's Creed Boss Hits Ubisoft With $1.3 million Lawsuit
description: Last fall, Ubisoft announced that Assassin's Creed executive producer Marc-Alexis Côté had left the company after spending two decades working his way up. Côté soon responded that he had been asked to "step aside," but added that he wasn't resentful toward Ubisoft. Now, Côté has filed a lawsuit against Ubisoft alleging that it mischaracterized his departure as voluntary in order to skip paying him severance and to keep his non-compete clause active. According to Video Games Chronicle, Côté is asking for $1.3 million in severance pay and moral damages. He is also asking the court to remove his non-compete clause. The lawsuit details Côté's side of the dispute, which contends that the issues between himself and Ubisoft began over Vantage Studios, a recently created subsidiarity in partnership with Tencent that will control the development of all Assassin's Creed, Rainbow Six, and Far Cry games. Côté contends that the positions he was offered at Vantage amounted to an "unacceptable demotion" that "did not carry the same scope, mandate, or continuity with the work I had been entrusted with in recent years." title: This Cyberpunk 2077 VR Mod Was Shut Down Because It Wasn't Free
description: A VR mod for Cyberpunk 2077 was struck down with a DMCA by CD Projekt Red because the mod's creator was charging for it. Luke Ross is a modder known for adding virtual reality support to games that do not natively have it. His Patreon subscribers pay him to access these mods, one of which was for Cyberpunk 2077. Earlier this month, though, CD Projekt Red issued a DMCA takedown, forcing Ross to remove the VR mod for this RPG that had previously been available. CD Projekt Red's VP of Business Development Jan Rosner confirmed in a post on X that the mod was taken down because it was paid, referencing the company's fan content guidelines. Marathon Sees Explosive Steam Sales Growth After Release Date Reveal
description: Following the reveal of its release date, Marathon has seen a surge of interest as PC players have begun locking in preorders for Bungie's sci-fi extraction shooter. At the time of writing, Marathon is the fifth-best-selling game on Steam in the US and 10th globally on the Steam Charts. Free-to-play games like Marvel Rivals and Counter-Strike 2 are ahead of it--only natural, given the low price of nothing for those titles--and Arc Raiders is still in the top spot for now. This is a positive step forward for the game, considering last year's controversy over alleged stolen art assets and the lukewarm reception since its reveal. It's also worth noting that Marathon will be available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S at launch, but sales data for those platforms isn't currently available to gauge player interest. Marathon was originally aiming to launch in September last year--a release date that would have brought it perilously close to the mega-successful Arc Raiders. It's now scheduled to launch on March 5, which gives it a fairly comfortable window to make its sales mark. The Steam preorders suggest it'll launch on PC with considerable momentum, but it remains to be seen whether it'll be able to hold onto its players in the highly competitive live-service games market. title: Hitman Is Getting Cross-Progression Soon As It Celebrates A Major Anniversary
description: In the five years since its release, Hitman: World of Assassination has hit multiple platforms, with Agent 47 infiltrating multiple PC storefronts, mobile devices, and even the original Switch through a cloud version of the game. In just a couple of weeks, players will be able to sync their progress across all platforms through cross-progression. Developer IO Interactive marked the stealth-action game's fifth anniversary with a blog post detailing how cross-progression will work once the feature goes live on February 3. Challenge progression, inventory, and even achievements will be stored online, ensuring that your experiences with Agent 47 seamlessly carry over no matter which platform you play on. The one caveat is that you can only pull from one "primary" save with cross-progression enabled. That's easy for anyone who perhaps owns Hitman on one platform and wants to switch to a new platform, but those who have saves on different platforms will have to choose just one of them to carry over. But if you're precious about each of your distinct saves, do know that cross-progression is reversible. Continue Reading at GameSpot
